claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be prepared as a homogeneous high-temperature BCC phase.
Phase stability in high-temperature BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is controlled by competition between an Al-induced thermodynamic ordering drive and diffusion-limited kinetics.
Al provides a thermodynamic driving force for atomic ordering in this alloy.
Slow cooling or isothermal holding permits enough diffusion to develop localized nanoscale B2-like ordered domains.
Formation of localized ordered regions destabilizes the disordered BCC state.
Rapid quenching kinetically preserves a metastable, disordered BCC phase.
Identically prepared samples should be compared after rapid quenching versus slow cooling or isothermal aging.
The treatments should be performed in a regime where diffusion is appreciable and the proposed Al-induced thermodynamic instability is significant.
At high temperature, Al is incorporated in disordered BCC despite having an unfavorable mixing free energy.
During slow cooling or aging, the free-energy reduction from ordering can overcome kinetic barriers and nucleate ordered or secondary phases.
Slow-cooled or aged samples will display additional XRD peaks attributable to ordering.
Slow-cooled or aged samples will contain nanoscale ordered domains observable by TEM.
Slow-cooled or aged samples will produce DSC signals associated with ordering transformations.
Rapidly quenched samples will remain a single disordered BCC phase with no detectable ordering or secondary phases.
Ordering will be suppressed when cooling is too rapid or the treatment temperature does not enter a diffusion-activated regime.
Changes away from Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 may alter phase-stability behavior.
Transformation kinetics and ordering extent may vary with processing details and small changes in experimental conditions.
A lack of ordering evidence after slow cooling or aging, or cooling-rate-independent transformation behavior, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
